claims.statement: Poland's deposit-return system began in October 2025; covered retailers collect deposits, larger shops accept returns, and system operators require agreements and records.
Independent retail chains may pay from store-operations budgets to reconcile deposits, returns, operator statements, and material pickups; actual budget is unknown.
The proposed transaction rail requires signed retailer and operator integrations; none are currently held.

commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: POS vendors and deposit operators can bundle reconciliation; cross-operator exception handling is the wedge
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed direct contracts with independent retail chains
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Direct outreach to regional chains, POS resellers, and waste-logistics firms

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Assumption: 8,000-25,000 PLN per chain through enterprise outbound and pilots
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Implementation fee upfront; platform fee monthly
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Assumption: 60-75% after integrations and exception support at mature deployments
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Assumption: 80-200 implementation hours per chain and ongoing settlement support
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Deposit-accounting review, security, data processing, and contractual liability; unknown
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Integration maintenance, transaction hosting, support, and partner commissions

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: POS suites and system operators expose bundled reconciliation modules
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Current cashier, finance, and logistics labor reconciling collected deposits, accepted packaging, operator settlements, and discrepancies
commercial_mechanics.payer: Regional grocery, convenience, or beverage retail chain
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Unreconciled deposit balances, growing return volume, or multiple-operator complexity
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Monthly if close time, discrepancies, and staff effort stay below baseline

contrary_evidence: Operators and POS suppliers may already cover most reconciliation.
Packaging bearing the deposit mark appeared gradually, delaying transaction density.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Proposed workflow-integration agreements with retailers and at least one deposit-system operator; unsigned
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Offer retailer-side CSV reconciliation without operator API access
critical_control_point.current_owner: Retailers, POS vendors, and licensed deposit-system operators control transaction records
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed direct contracts with independent retail chains
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: No present retail or operator data rights
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Prospective business only after counterparties grant integrations
critical_control_point.subject: Deposit-return reconciliation transaction rail

economics.acquisition_route: Validate with anonymized statement samples, build CSV reconciliation, and pursue one regional-chain pilot before API work
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Assumption: 3,000 stores at 250 PLN monthly equals 9m PLN ARR; even 15% owner earnings or a modest software multiple could support 5m PLN founder net worth in 6-10 years. Sales cycles and integration cost are unknown.
economics.founder_time: 20-25 hours weekly during pilot; implementation capacity must later be hired
economics.gross_margin_basis: Store subscriptions less integration support and transaction infrastructure
economics.payback: Assumption: 12-18 months due to enterprise acquisition and implementation costs
economics.pricing: Assumption: 10,000-40,000 PLN implementation plus 150-500 PLN per store monthly
economics.retention_or_repeat: Recurring while stores participate in the deposit system

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Exception mappings across POS systems and deposit operators
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Retail operations pays when deposit balances and returns require manual reconciliation
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A new deposit-marked packaging flow crosses checkout, return, logistics, and operator ledgers

founder_fit: Data reconciliation suits the founder's analytical background.
Can begin with CSV workflows before capital-intensive hardware.
Does not depend on a public personal brand.
risks: Operator API access may be refused.
Enterprise selling may exceed preferred social intensity.
Settlement errors could create financial liability.

structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: mapping between pos deposits returns and operator settlements
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: pos and deposit operator transaction exports

thesis: The newly operating deposit system creates a recurring cross-ledger reconciliation burden that is poorly served by single-system dashboards.
title: Deposit-Return Reconciliation Rail
uncertainties: Return-volume economics per store are unknown.
Operator data formats and access policies are unknown.
Retailers' current workaround costs are unknown.
